terra.problem: The passage does not say whether the visit included trumpets.
The passage says all Jerusalem was disturbed, not that the whole city was talking about the title.
“Wrong crown” uses “wrong” about the baker’s answer.
The passage does not establish that nobody in Jerusalem is asking about Persia.
The text says the Magi came from the east, but does not establish the length of their trip or that worship was their only purpose.
The text does not say whether Herod threw a party.
The line about nobody passing out cookies adds an unstated detail to the scene.
“Right after” adds timing the text does not give, and calling a meeting does not establish that someone cannot be unbothered.
The explanation ends by restating that the whole city means a lot of people. It is flat and adds no insight or personality.
The text identifies the writer as a prophet; it does not establish that he was not also a priest.
A staff in the ruler’s hand turns the shepherd description into a physical detail the prophecy does not give.
The birthplace has been identified, but the spot where the star appeared has not been settled.
“I’ll keep my own thoughts to myself and let the text speak” comments on how Papa tells the passage.
The text does not say whether the building under the star was nice-looking or famous.
The text does not establish whether the place where the Child was had a famous address.
The verse does not mention arguing or raised voices, but that does not establish that neither happened.
The text gives the warning received in the dream, but does not say that it was the only thing the dream covered.
The text reports the warning and the different route, but does not explicitly say the warning changed their intended path home.
